column5: context

Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway memory overread exposing session material. CVSS 7.5; in CISA KEV since 10 July 2025. The appliance flaw adversaries attempted to exploit most heavily this period, roughly nineteen times the next appliance signature. Carried in the 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27 briefs.

WordPress Core SQL injection. In CISA KEV; affects WordPress Core 6.8.x below 6.8.6, 6.9.x below 6.9.5 and 7.0.x below 7.0.2, where a plugin or theme passes untrusted input to the affected query parameter. Reported in the 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-27 briefs, absent from the two briefs since, resumed this period.

Cisco ASA and FTD web services file read. In CISA KEV. The vendor record bounds the read to files in the web services file system and states it cannot reach system or operating system files. Reconnaissance against the same platform ran far higher, with Cisco ASA Scanner at 405,464 probes.

Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile API authentication bypass reaching the mobile device management API. CVSS 5.3; in CISA KEV since 19 May 2025. Carried in the Finding 1 table. Paired with CVE-2025-4428 code injection at 70 attempts; CVE-2025-4428 requires authentication on its own, and chained behind CVE-2025-4427 it does not. Audit which API accounts can issue or revoke device credentials.

F5 BIG-IP configuration utility authentication bypass reaching arbitrary system commands. CVSS 9.8; in CISA KEV since 31 October 2023. A second GreyNoise signature for the same flaw fired 103 times in the window; both can fire on one request, so the higher count is carried. Exposure is via the management port and self IP addresses. First appearance in this brief series.

Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass. The documented impact is bypassing security restrictions to establish an unauthorized VPN connection. CVSS 9.1; in CISA KEV since 29 May 2026. Federal remediation deadline already elapsed. Critical, 24 to 48 hours. First appearance in this brief series.

Fortinet FortiClient EMS SQL injection. CVSS 9.8; in CISA KEV since 13 April 2026. High priority within 7 days; a product whose compromise would reach the endpoints it manages. Carried as a patch-priority item in the 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-24 briefs; adversaries attempted to exploit it this period, the first such attempts this series has recorded against it.

Citrix out-of-bounds read affecting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway when configured as a SAML IDP. CVSS 9.8; in CISA KEV since 30 March 2026. A second GreyNoise signature for the same flaw fired 54 times; the higher count of the pair is carried here. First appearance in this brief series.

Adobe ColdFusion path traversal that the vendor record scores as reaching arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, without user interaction; the GreyNoise tag describes the path as unauthenticated remote code execution through arbitrary file write operations. CVSS 10.0 with a changed scope; in CISA KEV since 7 July 2026. Affects ColdFusion 2025.9, 2023.20 and earlier. One of seventeen ColdFusion signatures active in the same window, so patching this flaw alone is unlikely to reduce attempt volume.

Ivanti Sentry unauthenticated operating system command injection reaching root-level code execution on an appliance fronting mobile device management. CVSS 10.0; in CISA KEV since 11 June 2026, so it enters the queue more than two months overdue. Critical, 24 to 48 hours. First appearance in this brief series.

Fortinet FortiWeb SQL injection, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized SQL code or commands. CVSS 9.8; in CISA KEV since 18 July 2025. One of three separate Fortinet products whose KEV-listed flaws adversaries attempted to exploit this period.
Fortinet FortiSandbox operating system command injection. CVSS 9.8; in CISA KEV since 16 July 2026. High priority within 7 days. First appearance in this brief series.
Ivanti Connect Secure command injection. In CISA KEV. Paired with CVE-2024-21893 server-side request forgery at 67 attempts, the deeper tail of Ivanti activity beneath the Sentry flaw.

AS215929, classified malicious. RDP crawling with 49,889 RDP Bruteforce Attempt sessions, 2% of its own connections. Paired with 192.253.248.251 on a shared JA4T; together 35% of all RDP crawling and 14% of all RDP credential attempts observed. Carried in the 2026-07-06, 2026-07-13, 2026-07-20, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-10 briefs; up roughly 16% per day against the last. Perishable, pair with the RDP Crawler and RDP Bruteforce Attempt tags.

AS201814, classified malicious, the only host of the ten-host port band sweep GreyNoise classifies as malicious. Owns the 1 to 3,000 band. The other nine members are classified unknown; resolve each in GreyNoise before acting.

AS208137, classified malicious. Secret and configuration file harvesting across 35 signatures; 425,532 ENV Crawler sessions, 8% of the corpus-wide ENV Crawler total of 5,299,656, plus 35% of TeleMessage CVE-2025-48927 and 32% of Laravel CVE-2024-29291 attempts. Carried since the 2026-06-22 brief; roughly 17% lower per day than the 2026-08-10 brief. Requests are GET only against ports 80, 443, 3000 and 8000, using more than 5,000 distinct fabricated user agent strings; that count is a measured floor and the true population is higher.

AS213790, classified malicious. Second RDP campaign, 18,749 RDP Bruteforce Attempt sessions, 1% of its own connections. Egresses through a commercial VPN service, so that provider carries the traffic and does not originate it. Carried in the 2026-08-10 brief.

column4: connection attempts from the ten named hosts in this range
column5: AS201814 MEVSPACE, 14 active hosts in the range; the ten profiled hosts produced 18,346,694 connection attempts, 6.2% of all traffic observed. Each swept a disjoint contiguous band. Nine tile 1 to 27,000 in exact 3,000-port strides ordered by last octet, and 45.141.233.148 holds the top of the range, 60,001 to 65,535; the ten bands span 32,535 of the 65,535 TCP ports. All ten first observed 12 August 2026. Only 45.141.233.145 is classified malicious and the other nine are unknown, so do not block the range: restrict the named hosts individually. No behavior tag isolates this cluster: seven of the ten carry no GreyNoise signature, and what the other three carry is protocol observations, Web Crawler, and one tail vulnerability check session between them. Web Crawler is the only one of those a blocklist would key on, and GreyNoise labels it unknown intent and does not recommend blocking it, so dynamic blocking cannot carry the control as these addresses rotate; detect on the contiguous run length and the shared JA4T instead. The range itself was reported in the 2026-02-06 brief for a different host, 45.141.233.32, at 1,168,476 RDP scanning probes.

column4: connection attempts from 213.209.159.175 carrying this user agent
column5: Fabricated Googlebot identification from 213.209.159.175, 232 of that host's 1,600,580 connection attempts, inside the same harvesting run. GreyNoise carries this behavior under the tag GoogleBot Pretender. The string is malformed, with two spaces and no plus before the URL where genuine Googlebot sends +http://, so it is matchable as written and must not be normalized. A second Googlebot-Mobile spoof string from the same host was also present, so 232 counts this one string and is not the host's total for Googlebot impersonation. Verify crawler claims by reverse DNS rather than by user agent string.
